concerns.text: FR-001 requires optical flow divergence ≤ 0.15 for inclusion of counterfactual pairs, but this threshold preferentially selects videos where the synthetic swap is visually similar to the original, introducing a selection bias that may artificially inflate ΔAcc reductions.

The design assumes an effect size d≈0.8 for the paired t‑test but provides no data‑driven justification; with only 5 random seeds the study is likely under‑powered, risking false‑negative conclusions.

ΔAcc is used as the primary indicator of ‘reliance on motion cues’, yet a lower ΔAcc could also result from the model simply ignoring object information rather than truly leveraging motion; no probing or ablation (e.g., removing motion features) is specified to disambiguate this.

The methodology mentions using frozen FlowNet‑C features for video representation but does not provide a citation or URL to the original FlowNet‑C model repository, violating the data‑resource citation requirement.

The Counterfactual Consistency Loss directly penalizes prediction changes on counterfactual pairs, which is exactly what the ΔAcc metric measures; evaluating ΔAcc reduction therefore constitutes a circular validation of the loss function.
